GRATITUDE.title: The Gift of Today
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you, God, for another morning. Not everyone woke up today — I did. That alone is something I did not earn.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What's one small thing today that usually goes unnoticed?

GRATITUDE.title: The People Around You
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the people in my life who show up in quiet ways — not always with words, but with presence.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Who made your life a little easier this week?

GRATITUDE.title: Your Body Carried You
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for a body that breathes without me asking. For a heart that kept going through every hard season.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What has your body handled lately that deserves a thank you?

GRATITUDE.title: The Hard Days
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you even for the hard days. They proved I was stronger than I believed. I made it through every single one.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Which difficult moment this year taught you something real?

GRATITUDE.title: Clean Water & Shelter
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for clean water. For shelter from the storm. For ordinary comforts I walk past without truly seeing.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Name one comfort you've been taking for granted.

GRATITUDE.title: This Breath
GRATITUDE.text: Right now, I am breathing. That means I am alive. That means there is still time — for healing, for love, for becoming.
GRATITUDE.prompt: If you had more time, what would you do more of?

GRATITUDE.title: The Learning
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for every mistake that taught me something. For every loss that showed me what truly mattered.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What do you know now that you didn't know a year ago?

GRATITUDE.title: Sunlight
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the light that finds its way in — through windows, through people, through unexpected moments of beauty.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What small moment of beauty did you witness today?

GRATITUDE.title: Second Chances
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for every new day — a fresh page. Not a reminder of what I failed, but a chance to begin again.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What would you do differently if today were a second chance?

GRATITUDE.title: Rest
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for sleep. For the quiet that holds us between one day and the next. For rest that asks nothing of us.
GRATITUDE.prompt: When did you last truly rest — mind and body both?

GRATITUDE.title: Kindness
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for every act of kindness I've received — the ones I remember and the ones I've forgotten. They all landed.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Who was unexpectedly kind to you recently?

GRATITUDE.title: Music
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for music. For a song that arrived at exactly the right moment. For the feeling of being understood by a stranger's melody.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What song has meant the most to you lately?

GRATITUDE.title: Growth
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for who I am becoming. Even slowly. Even imperfectly. I am not the same person I was a year ago.
GRATITUDE.prompt: How are you different from who you were 12 months ago?

GRATITUDE.title: Nourishment
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for food on the table. For the simple act of a meal. For energy that powers the life I'm building.
GRATITUDE.prompt: When did you last eat something that made you feel truly grateful?

GRATITUDE.title: Hands That Work
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for hands that can work, create, hold, and reach. For the ability to build something from nothing.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What have your hands made lately that you're proud of?

GRATITUDE.title: Someone Who Listened
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the person who listened when I needed to speak. For the one who made space for me.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Who do you feel truly heard by?

GRATITUDE.title: The Small Joys
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the small joys I almost missed — a warm cup, a good laugh, the feeling of sheets on tired skin.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Name three small things that brought you quiet joy this week.

GRATITUDE.title: My Mind
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for a mind that questions, wonders, and seeks. Even when it worries too much, it shows it cares.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What is your mind most curious about right now?

GRATITUDE.title: Healing
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for healing — physical, emotional, invisible. For the wounds that are slowly closing, even when I can't see them.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What part of you is healing right now, even if slowly?

GRATITUDE.title: Seasons That Change
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you that seasons change. That nothing stays the same forever — not the hard parts, not the waiting.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What season of life are you in right now?

GRATITUDE.title: Laughter
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for real laughter. The kind that catches you off guard. The kind that reminds you everything is not heavy.
GRATITUDE.prompt: When did you last laugh without holding back?

GRATITUDE.title: Hope
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for hope. For the small voice that says things can be different. For the part of me that keeps getting up.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What are you quietly hoping for right now?

GRATITUDE.title: Connection
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the connections that sustain me — family, friends, strangers who became more. For every relationship that held.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Who is one person you want to reach out to today?

GRATITUDE.title: Time
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for time. For hours that let me think, rest, build, and change. For every minute that hasn't run out yet.
GRATITUDE.prompt: How do you want to spend your time differently this week?

GRATITUDE.title: Nature
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the world outside — sky, trees, wind, water. For the simple truth that something bigger is still here.
GRATITUDE.prompt: When did you last stop to notice something in nature?

GRATITUDE.title: Creativity
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the urge to create — to write, cook, build, draw, dream. For the part of me that still wants to make something.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What do you wish you made more time to create?

GRATITUDE.title: Forgiveness
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the capacity to forgive — myself and others. For the relief that comes when I stop carrying what isn't mine.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Is there something you're ready to set down today?

GRATITUDE.title: Memories
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for memories that still make me smile. For the ones that remind me: I have been happy before. I will be again.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What's a memory that still warms you when you visit it?

GRATITUDE.title: Peace
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for every moment of genuine peace I have felt. For the proof that it exists. For the certainty it returns.
GRATITUDE.prompt: Where do you feel most at peace?

GRATITUDE.title: This Moment
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for now. For this exact moment — however ordinary or hard — because I am here in it, and that is everything.
GRATITUDE.prompt: If this moment was enough, what would that change?

GRATITUDE.title: The Journey
GRATITUDE.text: Thank you for the journey — not the destination, but the path. Every step shaped something in me.
GRATITUDE.prompt: What step have you taken recently that you're proud of?

AFFIRMATIONS: I am allowed to take up space and move at my own pace.
I do not need to earn rest. Rest is my right.
I am doing better than I think. I have survived every hard day so far.
I am not behind. I am exactly where I need to be right now.
I choose to release what I cannot control and breathe into what I can.
My feelings are valid. They are not permanent. They are just visiting.
I am worthy of peace — not because I earned it, but because I exist.
I am building something real. It takes time. That's okay.
I give myself permission to not have it all figured out today.
Every time I breathe and choose to continue, I am being brave.
I trust that I have what I need to get through today.
I am not my worries. I am the one noticing them.
There is strength in gentleness — especially toward myself.
I am allowed to ask for help. That is wisdom, not weakness.
Today, I show up as I am. That is more than enough.
My peace matters. I will protect it.
I have done hard things before. I can do hard things again.
I am growing even when it's invisible, even when it's slow.
I choose to be kind to myself today, in the small moments.
I am the calm beneath the storm. It is always there.
I deserve good things — not someday, but now.
What I feel is real. What I need matters. I will honor both.
I am not the worst thought I've had about myself.
Each breath I take is a fresh beginning.
I let go of the version of today I imagined. This version is enough.
I release perfectionism. Progress is the goal.
I am seen. I am loved. I belong here.
I will not rush my healing. Good things take time.
Today's difficulties are not permanent. They are passing through.
I am grateful for the small things — they are not small at all.
My story is not over. This is just one chapter.

CALM_STEPS.title: Release
CALM_STEPS.sub: Let go of tension in your body
CALM_STEPS.text:
Start at the very top...

• Let your forehead soften
• Unclench your jaw — let your tongue drop
• Drop your shoulders away from your ears
• Open your hands, uncurl your fingers
• Feel your feet heavy and flat on the floor

Notice how much your body was holding. Let it go.

CALM_STEPS.title: Ground Yourself
CALM_STEPS.sub: Come back to this exact moment
CALM_STEPS.text:
Look around slowly. Find:

5 things you can see right now
4 things you can physically feel
3 sounds you can hear
2 things you can smell
1 slow, complete breath

You are here. This room is real. You are safe inside this moment.

CALM_STEPS.title: Let One Thing Go
CALM_STEPS.sub: You don't have to carry everything
CALM_STEPS.text:
Think of one thing weighing on you right now.

You don't have to solve it. You don't have to fix it.

Just acknowledge it exists — and then choose, just for these next few minutes, to set it down outside the door.

Breathe in... and on the exhale, let it go.

CALM_STEPS.title: Your Affirmation
CALM_STEPS.sub: Read this slowly. Read it again.

NIGHT_STEPS.title: Set down today.
NIGHT_STEPS.body:
Whatever happened today — the mistakes, the unfinished things, the conversations that didn't go right — they don't travel with you into sleep.

Set them outside the door. You can pick them up tomorrow if you need to. Tonight, you rest.

NIGHT_STEPS.title: Soften your body.
NIGHT_STEPS.body:
Starting from the top:

• Relax your face completely
• Drop your shoulders
• Let your stomach soften
• Feel your legs grow heavy
• Let your arms rest with no effort

You are held. You are horizontal. You don't have to do anything.

NIGHT_STEPS.title: Breathe for sleep.
NIGHT_STEPS.body:
The 4-7-8 pattern naturally activates your body's rest mode.

Breath in for 4... hold for 7... breathe out completely for 8.

Three full cycles. Your body already knows what to do.

NIGHT_STEPS.title: One gratitude.
NIGHT_STEPS.body:
Think of one real thing from today you are grateful for.

It doesn't have to be big. A warm drink. A moment of quiet. The fact that you made it through.

Thank God for it. Hold it in your chest. Let it settle with you.

NIGHT_STEPS.title: You are allowed rest.
NIGHT_STEPS.body:
You are not behind. You did not fail today.

You showed up — in whatever way you could — and that is enough.

Close your eyes. Your body knows how to sleep. Your mind knows how to let go.

Good night.

segs.text:
Find a comfortable position.

Take a slow breath and settle in.

Take a slow breath in through your nose...

And let it all the way out.

Today is a new beginning.

Whatever yesterday held, it is behind you now.
This moment is completely fresh.

Breathe in again, and as you do, imagine breathing in clarity.

And as you breathe out... release anything that doesn't belong to today.

Think of one intention for today.

Not a goal. Not a task.

Just one word — one way you want to move through this day.

Let that word settle into your body.

You don't have to figure out how.
Just carry it gently.

Take one final deep breath...

And when you're ready, step into this day.

This day belongs to you.

MEDITATIONS.title: Anxiety Relief
MEDITATIONS.tagline: Immediate calm when you need it

segs.text:
You're here. That took courage.

Let's start with just one breath.

Breathe in slowly... 2... 3... 4...

And out slowly... 2... 3... 4... 5... 6.

Do that again.

Your nervous system just received a signal:

We are safe. We are here. We are okay.

Whatever you're feeling right now — it is not permanent.

It is a wave. You are not drowning. You are floating.

Look at one thing around you right now.

Something solid. Something real.

You are in a safe place.

Take another slow breath...

And say quietly to yourself:

"This will pass. It always does."

You are more capable than your anxiety believes.

You have gotten through every hard moment before this one.

You will get through this one too.

MEDITATIONS.title: Inner Stillness
MEDITATIONS.tagline: Find the quiet beneath the noise

segs.text:
Let everything go quiet for a moment.

You don't have to figure anything out right now.

Soften your gaze and let your shoulders drop.

Breathe slowly.

In... and out. Calm and easy.

Beneath all the thoughts, beneath all the noise...

there is a stillness that has always been there.

It belongs to you.

You don't have to earn access to this stillness.

You don't have to be perfect to feel it.

It's already here. It's always here.

Let your thoughts come and go like clouds.

You are not the cloud.

You are the sky.

Breathe into this feeling.

This is your natural state.

This is who you are beneath everything.

Carry this quiet with you.

Not as something fragile — but as something that cannot be taken.

It's yours.

MEDITATIONS.title: Heart of Gratitude
MEDITATIONS.tagline: Open your heart to what is good

segs.text:
Place one hand gently on your heart.

Feel it beating. That rhythm has never stopped for you.

Take a breath and with it, let gratitude begin to move through you.

Not forced. Not performed.

Just allowed.

Think of one person in your life who has loved you — even imperfectly.

Let yourself feel that love right now.

Think of one moment this week that was good.

It doesn't have to be big.

A warmth. A laugh. A small mercy.

Thank God for it.

Not because everything is perfect.

But because good things are real, and they deserve to be seen.

Let your chest fill with that feeling.

Gratitude is not just an emotion.

It is a way of seeing.

Take a deep breath in...

And breathe out slowly.

You have so much inside you. So much that is real and good.

The day is done.

You made it. Whatever it held — you made it through.

Take a slow breath in...

And as you breathe out, let the day begin to soften.

You did what you could today.

Some things went well. Some didn't.

All of it was enough.

Think of one thing that went right today.

Even something small.

Hold it for a moment.

Now think of something you're setting down tonight.

A worry. A regret. A conversation that still feels unfinished.

You don't have to carry it to bed.

Breathe in...

And breathe out, releasing it completely.

Tomorrow can hold what it needs to hold.

Let your body grow heavy.

Let your mind grow quiet.

You've done enough for today.

Rest now.

Good night.

Thank God for this day.

For the breath that carried you through it.

You are safe.

You are held.

You are allowed to rest completely.

Let your body grow heavy.

Let your breath slow.

There is nothing you need to do right now.

Breathe in for 4...

Hold for 7...

Breathe out for 8...

Your body is growing heavier with each breath.

Your muscles are letting go one by one.

You don't have to hold anything.

Let your thoughts drift by like gentle clouds.

You don't need to follow them.

Just watch them pass.

You are safe in this moment.

The world will continue while you sleep.

You are allowed to leave it for a while.

Feel the weight of your body being held.

You don't have to hold yourself up anymore.

Let go completely.

Breathe in gently...

And breathe out... slowly... completely...

Sleep is coming.

Thank God for this rest.

For this quiet.

For this safe place to lay your head.

Good night.

CRISIS_DATA.b: Whatever is happening — stop. Don't try to fix it right now. Just stop moving for one moment.
Put your hand on your chest. Feel it rise. Breathe in through your nose... slowly out through your mouth. Again.

What are you feeling right now? Say it out loud or in your mind.

"I feel ___." Naming it is the first step to moving through it.
This feeling is not permanent. You have felt this before and come through it. You are stronger than this moment.

You don't need to fix everything. Just one tiny thing: drink water, step outside, text someone.

One step is enough.

JPROMPTS: What happened today that I want to remember?
How did I feel today — really?
What am I grateful for right now, even if small?
What's one thing I'd tell myself tomorrow morning?

c: Your brain isn't broken. It's overwhelmed. There's a big difference.
Every day, your brain processes thousands of pieces of information — emails, decisions, worries. It's doing enormous invisible work.
When things pile up, your brain's alarm system fires. It doesn't care about logic. It just sees pressure.
That feeling of 'I can't think straight'? That's your alarm drowning out your rational mind.
The solution isn't to think harder. It's to slow down just enough so your calm mind can come back online.
You are not too much. You are overloaded. And overloaded systems just need to pause.
Anxiety isn't weakness. It's your brain being too good at its job.
Your brain runs a simulation — asking 'what could go wrong?' Not because something is wrong, but to protect you.
It can't tell the difference between a real danger and an email you're nervous about. Both trigger the same alarm.
So your heart races. Your chest tightens. Your thoughts loop. None of that means something bad is happening.
The way out isn't to fight it. It's to send your brain a calm signal: we're safe. We're here.
Anxiety is a messenger. Not a verdict.

LEARN_DATA.t: How to Calm Your Thoughts Fast
c: When thoughts are racing, the worst thing you can do is fight them.
Name what you feel specifically — 'I feel scared that I'm going to fail.' Naming activates your rational mind.
Breathe out longer than you breathe in. Try 4 counts in, 6 counts out. Your nervous system has a brake pedal.
Look around and name 3 real things you can see. This pulls you out of your head and back into the room.
Say one true thing: 'I am here. This feeling will pass. I have made it through hard things before.'
Done fully, it takes 60 seconds. The goal is to slow down enough that you're driving again.

LEARN_DATA.t: When Your Mind Won't Stop Looping
c: You've been in bed for an hour. Your brain won't stop. The same thoughts, over and over.
Your brain is stuck in problem-solving mode — running the same loop hoping to find the answer.
The way to break the loop isn't to solve the problem. It's to give your brain something different to do.
Write down every thought. Your brain will stop running it because it feels 'stored.'
Change your physical position. Stand up. Splash water on your face.
Accept you might not solve it tonight. Some things need sleep, not more thinking.

overwhelmed.msg: You don't have to solve everything right now.
overwhelmed.sub: One breath. One step. That's all this moment needs.

stressed.msg: Stress means you care about something.
stressed.sub: Let's give that energy somewhere to land.

tired.msg: Your mind has worked hard today.
tired.sub: You have permission to rest. Right now.

calm.msg: Good. Let's protect and deepen that.
calm.sub: A moment of calm is worth honoring.
